CARB values diversity at all levels of the organization and is committed to fostering an environment where employees from various backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. CARB believes the diversity of our employees collectively makes up one of the world’s most respected environmental organizations. CARB offers various modern interview options, including remote phone and video interviews. Join CARB and help us improve the lives of all Californians.

Job Description And Duties

The mission of the Chemical Analysis and Emissions Research Branch is to timely provide accurate measurements of mobile source emissions and fuels and technical expertise to support the California Air Resources Board (CARB) motor vehicle and clean fuels programs.

The Fuel Analysis and Methods Evaluation Section (FAMES) is looking for an individual with strong work ethics, strong background in analytical chemistry, and good communication skills. The section analyzes motor vehicle fuels at the Southern California Head Quarters in Riverside. The results are used in determining compliance with the cleaner burning gasoline and clean diesel regulations. FAMES also provides support to the Motor Vehicle Program by analyzing fuels used in emissions testing and providing expertise on the impact of fuel properties on emissions. Both functions require the evaluation, development, and implementation of more precise and accurate methods of analysis. FAMES is also responsible for proposing the adoption of new and updated methods into California regulations.

Under the direction of the FAMES Manager, the Staff Air Pollution Specialist serves as an independent technical expert to oversee fuels analyses and methods. In addition, the incumbent will apply engineering principles to perform the more complex work of evaluating fuel effects on vehicle emissions and develop test methods for the fuel regulations when the need arises. Duties include evaluating and improving fuel analysis test methods; conducting fuel sample analysis; and overseeing the fuel analysis work conducted by other staff, conducting second-level quality control on reported data, reviewing literature studies related to fuel effect issues, and developing test plans to investigate fuel impacts. The incumbent will be responsible for data analysis, interpretation, reports, and oral presentations to stakeholders. The incumbent may also act as an expert witness for CARB or any related court action.

The following are requirements of the position:

Must maintain a good driving record.
A certification of completed Defensive Driver Training.
Participation in the DMV Pull Notice Program and a sustained good driving record.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

The position(s) require(s) a valid California Drivers License (CDL). You must answer the questions addressing your CDL on your application. Ensure you provide your CDL number, class, expiration date, and any endorsements and/or restrictions.

Applicants must include a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ) for this recruitment. The SOQ is a narrative discussion prepared by the applicant describing how their skills, knowledge, abilities, education, training, and experience qualify them for the position. The SOQ documents each candidate’s ability to present information clearly and concisely in writing. Candidates whose applications do not include the required SOQ will not be considered for this position. Resumes do not take the place of the SOQ.

jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Manager
jobs.description:
Our client is seeking an experienced Environmental Compliance Manager
to support environmental compliance activities across multiple projects and operating facilities throughout California.

This position will combine environmental leadership with hands-on technical compliance responsibilities. The Environmental Compliance Manager will support projects through various stages of development, construction, and operations while working closely with internal project teams, field personnel, consultants, and regulatory agencies.

The ideal candidate will bring a strong background in environmental permitting and compliance within energy, construction, infrastructure, industrial operations, or another highly regulated environment. This individual should be comfortable interpreting complex environmental requirements, providing direction to others, managing multiple priorities, and ensuring compliance requirements are effectively implemented in the field.

Responsibilities

Lead and coordinate environmental compliance activities across multiple project and operational sites.
Provide technical guidance and direction to environmental personnel, consultants, contractors, and project teams.
Support environmental compliance throughout pre-construction, construction, and ongoing operations.
Review environmental permits, plans, mitigation measures, and regulatory requirements and translate them into practical field requirements.
Oversee field inspections, compliance documentation, regulatory reporting, corrective actions, and permit obligations.
Support compliance programs involving stormwater and water quality, wildlife and biological resources, spill prevention, air quality, hazardous materials, and waste.
Coordinate with regulatory and resource agencies and support agency inspections, meetings, and compliance responses.
Track environmental commitments, permit conditions, reporting deadlines, corrective actions, and other compliance obligations.
Review environmental reports, field documentation, regulatory submissions, and technical work products.
Coordinate environmental consultants and technical service providers.
Develop practical environmental procedures, training materials, checklists, and field tools.
Identify potential environmental compliance risks and work with internal stakeholders to develop appropriate corrective and preventive actions.
Support environmental permitting and due diligence activities associated with new and existing projects.
Maintain organized and accurate environmental compliance records.
Travel to project and operating sites throughout California as needed.

﻿

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Natural Resources, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
5+ years of progressive environmental compliance experience within energy, construction, infrastructure, industrial operations, or a comparable environment.
Experience leading environmental programs, projects, field teams, or environmental professionals.
Strong understanding of federal, state, and local environmental regulations and permitting requirements.
Experience interpreting environmental permits and implementing requirements in active field environments.
Experience with construction and/or operational environmental compliance.
Knowledge of stormwater/SWPPP, spill prevention, hazardous materials and waste, air quality, water quality, and environmental permitting.
Experience with wildlife, biological resources, mitigation monitoring, and resource agency permitting is highly desirable.
Experience interacting with regulatory agencies and environmental consultants.
Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple sites, deadlines, and priorities.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently while providing leadership and direction to others.
Ability to travel regularly throughout California, including occasional overnight travel.

Help shape the future of clean transportation and energy efficiency in California!

The California Energy Commission (CEC) is looking for a Replacement Tire Efficiency Specialist to join the Fuels and Transportation Division’s Regulations and Legislative Unit. This is an exciting opportunity to help advance California’s clean transportation goals while supporting the implementation of the state’s Replacement Tire Efficiency Program.

-Telework schedule approved for candidates within California
-Salary Ranges:

In this role, you’ll evaluate emerging vehicle, fueling infrastructure, alternative fuel, and tire efficiency technologies; develop innovative and cost-effective strategies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, toxic air pollutants, and fuel consumption; and work closely with tire manufacturers, government agencies, technical experts, and public stakeholders. You may also serve as a team lead and help shape the long-term direction of a high-profile program through project management, technical assistance, incentives, policy development, education, and outreach.

We’re looking for someone who can bring strong project management and communication skills, work effectively across teams and organizations, and confidently engage with agency leadership, industry partners, and the public. Experience with energy efficiency programs, tires or related products, or customer-facing programs is highly desirable.
